credential_type.quote: the board shall grant a license to practice medicine to an applicant

is_mandatory.quote: Prior to the approval of a license, the applicant shall not engage in the practice of medicine in this state, and any person who practices medicine in this state without first obtaining approval of a license shall be deemed to have violated the provisions of this article 240.

title_protection.quote: Using the title "M.D.", "D.O.", "physician", "surgeon", or any word or abbreviation to indicate or induce others to believe that one is licensed to practice medicine in this state

scope_protection.quote: If a person who does not possess and has not filed a license to practice medicine, practice as a physician assistant, or practice as an anesthesiologist assistant in this state, as provided in this article 240, and who is not exempted from the licensing requirements under this article 240, performs any of the acts that constitute the practice of medicine as defined in this section, the person shall be deemed to be practicing medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Resorting to fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for, securing, renewing, or seeking reinstatement of a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Resorting to fraud, misrepresentation, or deception in applying for, securing, renewing, or seeking reinstatement of a license to practice medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of an offense of moral turpitude, a felony, or a crime that would constitute a violation of this article
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any conviction of an offense of moral turpitude, a felony, or a crime that would constitute a violation of this article 240.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Administering, dispensing, or prescribing any habit-forming drug or controlled substance other than in the course of legitimate professional practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Administering, dispensing, or prescribing any habit-forming drug or any controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-102 (5) other than in the course of legitimate professional practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution, or use of any controlled substance
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any conviction of violation of any federal or state law regulating the possession, distribution, or use of any controlled substance

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual or excessive use or abuse of alcohol, a habit-forming drug, or a controlled substance
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual or excessive use or abuse of alcohol, a habit-forming drug, or a controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-102 (5)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or abetting in the practice of medicine any person not licensed to practice medicine or whose license is suspended
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The aiding or abetting, in the practice of medicine, of any person not licensed to practice medicine as defined under this article 240 or of any person whose license to practice medicine is suspended

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing medicine as partner, agent, or employee of a person who does not hold a license to practice medicine
disciplinary_grounds.quote: practicing medicine as the partner, agent, or employee of, or in joint venture with, any person who does not hold a license to practice medicine within this state

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violating or attempting to violate any provision or term of this article 240
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violating, or attempting to violate, directly or indirectly, or assisting in or abetting the violation of or conspiring to violate any provision or term of this article 240

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to notify the board of a physical illness, condition, or behavioral/mental health disorder that impacts ability to practice safely
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to notify the board, as required by section 12-30-108 (1), of a physical illness, physical condition, or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder that impacts the licensee's ability to perform a medical service with reasonable skill and safety to patients

disciplinary_grounds.description: Any act or omission that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Any act or omission that fails to meet generally accepted standards of medical practice

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in a sexual act with a patient during the course of patient care or within six months following termination of the professional relationship
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in a sexual act with a patient during the course of patient care or within six months immediately following the termination of the licensee's professional relationship with the patient.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Refusal of an attending physician to comply with the terms of a patient's declaration and failure to transfer care
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Refusal of an attending physician to comply with the terms of a declaration executed by a patient pursuant to the provisions of article 18 of title 15 and failure of the attending physician to transfer care of the patient to another physician

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of abuse of health insurance statutes or advertising to perform prohibited acts
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of abuse of health insurance pursuant to section 18-13-119

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of any valid board order or any rule promulgated by the board
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of any valid board order or any rule promulgated by the board in conformance with law

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Dispensing, injecting, or prescribing an anabolic steroid, as defined in section 18-18-102 (3), for the purpose of the hormonal manipulation that is intended to increase muscle mass, strength, or weight without a medical necessity

disciplinary_grounds.description: Prescribing, distributing, or giving controlled substances to a family member or to oneself except on an emergency basis
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Prescribing, distributing, or giving to a family member or to oneself except on an emergency basis any controlled substance as defined in section 18-18-204

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the board, within thirty days after an adverse action, that an adverse action has been taken against the licensee by another licensing agency in another state or country

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to report to the board within thirty days the surrender of a license or membership while under investigation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to report to the board, within thirty days, the surrender of a license or other authorization to practice medicine in another state or jurisdiction

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing to accurately answer the questionnaire accompanying the renewal form
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to accurately answer the questionnaire accompanying the renewal form as required pursuant to section 12-240-130 (2)

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willful and repeated ordering or performance, without clinical justification, of demonstrably unnecessary laboratory tests or studies; the administration, without clinical justification, of treatment that is demonstrably unnecessary

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Falsifying or repeatedly making incorrect essential entries or repeatedly failing to make essential entries on patient records

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Committing a fraudulent insurance act, as defined in section 10-1-128

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing to establish and continuously maintain financial responsibility, as required in section 13-64-301

disciplinary_grounds.quote: The discipline of a license to practice medicine, of a license to practice as a physician assistant, or of a license to practice as an anesthesiologist assistant in another state, territory, or country shall be deemed to be unprofessional conduct.

definition_quote.value: "practice of medicine" means: (a) Holding out one's self to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease; ailment; pain; injury; deformity; physical condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever
definition_quote.quote: "practice of medicine" means: (a) Holding out one's self to the public within this state as being able to diagnose, treat, prescribe for, palliate, or prevent any human disease; ailment; pain; injury; deformity; physical condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder, whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

value: interpretation of tests including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs
methods_authorized.quote: whether by the use of drugs, surgery, manipulation, electricity, telemedicine, the interpretation of tests, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, images, or photographs, or any physical, mechanical, or other means whatsoever

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe, administer, and dispense drugs including controlled substances in the course of legitimate professional practice; subject to opioid prescribing limits and electronic prescribing requirements.
drug_authority.quote: Suggesting, recommending, prescribing, or administering any form of treatment, operation, or healing for the intended palliation, relief, or cure of a person's physical disease; ailment; injury; condition; or behavioral, mental health, or substance use disorder

license_status_types.quote: Any licensee pursuant to section 12-240-117 may apply to the board to be transferred to an inactive status.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: International medical graduates must complete one year of postgraduate clinical training approved by the board. If the international medical school is not an approved medical college, the applicant may still be eligible at board discretion if they hold specialty board certification from ABMS or AOA.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: For international medical graduates, the board shall require one year of postgraduate clinical training approved by the board. An applicant whose international medical school is not an approved medical college is eligible for licensure at the discretion of the board if the applicant meets all other requirements for licensure and holds specialty board certification

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: Has completed either an approved internship of at least one year or at least one year of postgraduate training approved by the board.

pain_management_education_required.quote: the regulator for each licensed health-care provider, in consultation with the center for research into substance use disorder prevention, treatment, and recovery support strategies created in section 27-80-118, shall promulgate rules that require each licensed health-care provider, as a condition of renewing, reactivating, or reinstating a license on or after October 1, 2022, to complete up to four credit hours of training per licensing cycle in order to demonstrate competency regarding: (I) Best practices for opioid prescribing
pain_management_education_required.citation: UMBRELLA / Article 30 - Provisions Applicable to Health-Care Profession

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: A prescriber shall not prescribe more than a seven-day supply of an opioid to a patient who has not obtained an opioid prescription from that prescriber within the last twelve months, with exceptions for chronic pain, cancer-related pain, post-surgical pain expected to last more than 14 days, and palliative/hospice care.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: A prescriber shall not prescribe more than a seven-day supply of an opioid to a patient who has not obtained an opioid prescription from that prescriber within the last twelve months and may exercise discretion to include a second fill for a seven-day supply.
opioid_prescribing_limits.citation: UMBRELLA / Article 30 - Provisions Applicable to Health-Care Profession

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: Each prescriber licensed in this state who holds a current registration issued by the federal drug enforcement administration shall register and maintain a user account as specified in section 12-280-403.
controlled_substance_database_registrati.citation: UMBRELLA / Article 30 - Provisions Applicable to Health-Care Profession

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: Telemedicine is authorized as part of the practice of medicine. Professional practice standards applicable to in-person care apply to telehealth, including prescribing standards. Registered out-of-state telehealth providers may not prescribe controlled substances.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The delivery of telemedicine. Nothing in this subsection (1)(g) authorizes physicians to deliver services outside their scope of practice

telemedicine_license_available.quote: On and after January 1, 2026, an applicant who possesses an out-of-state credential may provide health-care services through telehealth to patients located in this state if the applicant is registered with a regulator
telemedicine_license_available.citation: UMBRELLA / Article 30 - Provisions Applicable to Health-Care Profession

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: To facilitate the licensure of a physician under the "Interstate Medical Licensure Compact Act", part 36 of article 60 of title 24, the board shall obtain a set of fingerprints from an applicant for licensure under the compact

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician assistant may not provide care unless the physician assistant has entered into a collaborative agreement with a physician licensed in good standing pursuant to this article 240 or article 290 of this title 12 or a physician group.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may prescribe and dispense medication, including controlled substances, to the extent and in the manner authorized by board rules, within the scope of their collaborative agreement.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: a physician assistant licensed by the board pursuant to section 12-240-113 may perform acts within the physician assistant's education, experience, and competency that constitute the practice of medicine and acts that physicians are authorized by law to perform to the extent and in the manner authorized by rules promulgated by the board, including prescribing and dispensing medication, including controlled substances.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: An instance of a medical malpractice settlement or judgment against a licensee reported to the board pursuant to section 10-1-120

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Disciplinary actions taken by hospitals to suspend or revoke the privileges of a physician and reported to the board pursuant to section 25-3-107

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The board shall select one or more peer health assistance programs as designated providers. To be eligible for designation by the board, a peer health assistance program must: (I) Provide for the education of physicians, physician assistants, and anesthesiologist assistants with respect to the recognition and prevention of physical, emotional, and psychological problems

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: If the board has reasonable cause to believe that a licensee is unable to practice with reasonable skill and safety to patients because of a condition described in section 12-240-121 (1)(e) or (1)(i), it may require the licensee to submit to mental or physical examinations by physicians designated by the board.
